questions.stem: All hormones react to a negative feedback except:
questions.why: Oxytocin operates via a positive feedback loop (e.g., uterine contractions stimulate more oxytocin release).

notes.C: Prolactin feeds back negatively by raising hypothalamic dopamine.

questions.stem: When a patient with diabetes insipidus is treated successfully with antidiuretic hormone the:

options.label: A
options.text: urinary flow rate should fall by about 50 per cent

options.label: B
options.text: urinary output should be reduced to around 1 ml/minute

options.label: C
options.text: urinary osmolality should rise to between 100 and 200 mOsm/litre

options.label: E
options.text: salt intake should be carefully regulated

questions.why: Untreated diabetes insipidus produces 10–20 L of dilute urine a day (about 7–14 ml/min). With ADH the collecting ducts reabsorb water again, so urine output falls to the normal ~1 ml/min and urine becomes concentrated.

notes.A: Urine flow falls much more than 50%.
notes.C: Urine becomes concentrated, well above plasma (about 300 mOsm).
notes.D: Plasma osmolality FALLS back to normal as water is retained.
notes.E: Salt restriction is not part of ADH treatment.
